10A.
Report from the Urban Agriculture Subcommittee. Contact Persons: Deputy Mayor Kranz and Council Member Shaffer.
A. Receive the report.
B. Discuss the major concepts and structure of the proposed ordinance and give staff direction on these questions:
1) Should staff develop a new urban agriculture ordinance to reduce regulations and increase the threshold for by-right (no permit required) agriculture and agriconnection activities in residential zones?
2) Should staff develop a new streamlined permit process for urban agriculture and agriconnection activities with reduced fees and reduced processing requirements?
3) Is the proposed definition of "agriconnection activities" appropriate? Specifically, should art lessons, yoga, dance, or music be included?
4) Other general feedback on the proposed framework?
C. Give staff direction to proceed with development of formal ordinance language for Planning Commission and Council review and approval, based on input received above, or give direction to do something else related to urban agriculture.
D. Discuss and give direction on the additional recommendations, i.e.,
1) Encourage HOAs and landlords to allow food cultivation
anywhere on private property and in common areas, consistent with the proposed new ordinance.
2) Direct staff to bring back City Council Policy C025 for revisions, including the effective establishment of a citywide Integrated Pest Management practice.
3) Direct staff to present an update on direction Council approved in 2011 as part of the Environmental Action Plan, which said: "Expand upon and regularly review the City's Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program to seek more cost efficient, less toxic and alternative IPM practices for municipal facilities/lands. To show City's leadership efforts, list current IPM efforts on www.EncinitasEnvironment.org by Fall 2011. Public Works and Parks & Recreation Departments will provide a presentation to Council on the IPM program."
4) Take appropriate action modeled on the examples from Seattle, Spokane and Shorewood regarding bees and neonicotinoids, in the context of our Integrated Pest Management policies.
5) Provide education and strongly encourage use of organic practices. Terms such as "organic practices" and "toxic substances" will need to be defined carefully to address our policy goals and not generate unintended negative impacts.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
